newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek national airline buys 3 Avro RJ-85 planes.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek national airline buys 3 Avro RJ-85 planes.

text.p: Uzbekistan's national airline has signed a contract to buy three Avro RJ-85 aeroplanes and is planning to purchase an Airbus A310 jetliner, a senior official from the airline said on Friday.
Uzbekistan Khavo Yullari's deputy chief executive Valery Tyan gave no further details on the purchase of the three 80-seater aircraft made by British Aerospace Plc.
He said negotiations were underway for the purchase of an Airbus A-310. The former Soviet republic already flies two A-310s, leased in 1993, on international routes including Delhi and London.
Earlier, the airline said the RJ-85s would replace ageing Soviet-era Antonov AN-24s and Tupolev Tu134s and would fly domestic and Asian routes.
Tyan added the first of two Boeing 767s, ordered along with a Boeing 757 for a total of $220 million by the airline last year, would be delivered next week.
